This review ran the fence's own gate at the reviewed base 520cddc6 and head b72dcfab in scratch trees of each revision: both arms EXIT=0, 40 and 46 passed. added_failure_count 0 with ids [].

findings.text: follow-on: _supply_emitted_probe_angles binds the emitted magnetics/b_field_pol_probe/poloidal_angle array to the mapped probes by position (zip(probe_indices, angles, strict=True) at :125), assuming the emitted array's element order equals the order geometry_adapter._b_probes:165 builds b_probe sensor_map entries in (families by first-seen index, then item). The count check at :118 refuses a size mismatch, so a multi-family split is caught, but a same-length array whose elements are permuted relative to the probes would be silently mis-assigned; no test varies the order.

follow-on: the unit selection is a two-way branch — np.rad2deg(values) only when emitted.target_unit == 'rad' (:123); every other spelling, including None or an unrecognised unit, passes the raw values through as degrees rather than refusing. A mis-declared target_unit therefore mis-scales every probe angle silently. The DD leaf is radians, so the branch is correct for the intended binding, but a reader that accepted exactly the {rad, deg, degree} vocabulary and refused the rest would not guess a unit; no test drives a non-rad, non-degree unit.

follow-on: _poloidal_angle_sense_factor (:435) accepts only identity and negate and refuses every other value, including not-applicable, whereas the generic _apply_sign_convention:397 treats not-applicable as identity. The divergence is defensible — a directed angle must declare a sense — but it is stated in neither the binding schema nor the fragment, so a probe-angle binding authored not-applicable is refused at emit time with a message naming pol_angle_like; worth a comment or a schema note.

follow_ons: the JT-60SA catalogue's own poloidal_angle binding is outside this node's write scope (the fragment says so), so the description route stays inert for JT-60SA until the vacuum adjudication authors that binding; no action for this node.

the positional binding of the emitted angle array to the probes (finding at description_reader.py:125) and the two-way unit branch (:123) are unguarded; a follow-on test node should add an order-varying and a non-rad unit case when the JT-60SA description route first becomes live.
the plan section 6 assigns the angle-vs-wall axis repair to jtmm-probe-axis-store in imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py, a path outside this review's fence, so its correctness is not assessed here.
